description: The export's processing and encoders (src/export/encode.h, padding.h, png_writer.h, exr_writer.h; decisions 089 and 090): Painter's PNG and OpenEXR files re-encoded byte for byte, the recorded processing written by WriteExport byte-identical to Painter's files, and the processing no recording covers yet.

entries.subject: PNG files: chunks, row filters and compression of Painter's PNG export
entries.formula: Signature; IHDR (8 or 16 bits; grey, RGB or RGBA; not interlaced); pHYs 2835 x 2835 per metre; IDAT chunks of 8192 bytes (the last shorter) holding one zlib stream (level 6, window bits 15, memory level 8, strategy Z_FILTERED) of the filtered rows; IEND. Each row takes, among None, Sub and Paeth only, the filter whose bytes have the smallest sum of min(b, 256 - b), ties to the earlier; the row above the first is zero (src/export/png_writer.h, decision 089).

entries.subject: OpenEXR files: header, channels and PIZ compression of Painter's OpenEXR export
entries.formula: Single-part scanline file, version 2; attributes channels, compression (PIZ), dataWindow, displayWindow, lineOrder (increasing y), pixelAspectRatio 1, screenWindowCenter (0, 0), screenWindowWidth 1; FLOAT channels Y (grey), B, G, R (RGB) or A, B, G, R (RGBA); PIZ as OpenEXR writes it, its Huffman heap breaking frequency ties by symbol (tinyexr with that local change, src/export/exr_writer.h, decision 089).

entries.subject: PNG 16: the written code of each exported value
entries.formula: code = (j 65535 + 2^19 - 1) >> 20 with j = floor(clamp(v, 0, 1) 2^20) (arith::WriteUnorm), every channel as the evaluator reads it out; the files written by WriteExport equal Painter's byte for byte.

entries.notes: Not the nearest covered texel: on tier0/semantics/height-normal-bevelled-cube (Height) 12040 of the 12200 uncovered texels differ from it. Partial fit (decision 090): an 8-neighbour copy dilation (first covered neighbour: right, left, up, down, then the diagonals; x wraps, y does not) is exact on the bevelled cube's virtual normals (12200 gutter texels) and misses 32 to 44 texels per sphere normal map at the poles; a document channel's one-texel ring around each island blends across the UV seam with unidentified weights (2344 ring texels on the cube, 2152 on the sphere). Passthrough on such sets is written as no operation: Painter's r1 and r2 agree inside the islands and differ outside them at up to every uncovered texel.
